newsitem.title: USA: Callaway Golf buys Odyssey from US Industries.
newsitem.headline: Callaway Golf buys Odyssey from US Industries.

text.p: Callaway Golf Co. said Monday it agreed to buy all of the assets of Odyssey Sports Inc. from US Industries Inc. for $130 million in cash.
U.S. Industries said that as a result of the sale it expects to net proceeds of about $80 million and generate an after-tax gain of about $50 million.
Odyssey, based in Carlsbad, Calif., makes the Odyssey line of premium putters that are favoured on the Senior PGA and Ladies PGA Tours, Nike Tour and PGA Tour.
Callaway makes Big Bertha metal woods and irons, including the No. 1 drivers in use on the PGA, Senior PGA, Ladies PGA, Nike and European PGA Tours, it said.
"Last year, Callaway decided that by the end of 1997 we wanted to provide the golfing public with the best performing putter in the market," said Donald Dye, president and CEO of Callaway.

"The acquisition will also add to shareholder value and provide Callaway Golf with an opportunity to effectively compete, worldwide, for putter business against established, well-known putter brands such as Ping, Titleist, Ram and others."
The deal is subject to governmental reviews. An expected closing date has not been announced, Callaway said.
Callaway's stock edged up 19 cents to $37.625, while US Industries was unchanged at $40.06 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
